node: Critical energy supplier-risk management, resilience, testing, certification, and procurement intelligence
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a small set of US-listed names plausibly tied to the shadow lane around energy supplier-risk complexity, grid resilience analytics, asset integrity testing, and certification gates. The cleanest node exposures are not classic power-equipment manufacturers; they are testing/inspection/certification providers and consulting/data firms that utilities, developers, OEMs, and industrial energy customers may need when supply chains, compliance, reliability, and project execution risk become structural. Moody's is included only as a reference anchor because its current supplier-risk messaging directly frames the node, while TIC Solutions, ICF, and UL Solutions form the more investable discovery set. The evidence is still early: later layers should verify energy/utility revenue mix, recurring vs project revenue, customer concentration, backlog, and whether services are actually tied to supplier qualification or asset-integrity chokepoints rather than generic consulting/TIC activity.
